title: r/longevity - Senolytic Therapies Pose Revolutionary Potential to Roll Back Diseases of Aging
abstract:
It's kind of perplexing how there can be such different results in various lines/stages of research. In the Interventions Testing Program, fisetin was found to have no effect on median or maximum lifespan in treated mice compared to controls.
If fisetin were senolytic, and if removing senescent cells were beneficial, I would expect some difference between the treated groups and controls in median or maximum lifespan.
